entry.title: [VahidOnline] Pezeshkian: We will not shy away from negotiating for peace. Masoud Pezeshkian,…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @VahidOnline

Pezeshkian: We will not shy away from negotiating for peace. Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of government in the Islamic Republic, said in his speech on Wednesday, the first of Mehr, at the 81st United Nations General Assembly that he had prepared the text of his speech in advance, but after the remarks of Donald Trump, the President of the United States, and his calling the Islamic Republic a "terrorist," he decided to show the audience a photo of Ali Khamenei, the killed leader of the Islamic Republic, and the students of the Minab school. Pezeshkian also said: "Anyone they want to destroy, they label a terrorist. For 200 years, Iran has not attacked any country and has only defended itself, but they call us a source of insecurity." In another part of his remarks, he said: "America and Israel attacked us with the latest equipment, and we defended ourselves with power." Pezeshkian said America and Israel imposed war on Iran, but the Islamic Republic defended "with power" and at the same time "does not shy away from negotiating for peace." Regarding the Islamic Republic's nuclear program, he said: "To defend our country, we do not seek permission from anyone. Iran does not accept that nuclear knowledge be monopolized by a few countries; we do not consider nuclear weapons a factor of security." Pezeshkian continued regarding the Strait of Hormuz: "It is not possible for everyone to benefit from the Strait of Hormuz while the shipping route for Iran is closed. The deployment of hostile fleets and the expansion of war do not bring security to shipping." Regarding the conditions of the region, he also said: "We live in a region where war knows no borders and the crisis of one country spreads to its neighbors. Therefore, we consider our neighbors strong." @VahidOnLive

Pezeshkian: Either we build security together or we endure insecurity together. Masoud Pezeshkian at the United Nations General Assembly said: "A peace that is not for everyone is not peace. Either we will build security together or we will endure insecurity together. We are ready for dialogue, but we will not accept the language of force." He added: "Trump's remarks, in the eyes of global public opinion and thinkers, are a clear sign of a bullying nature and the logic of force and contrary to the explicit charter of the United Nations." Pezeshkian said: "Trump should know that these remarks make our nation more cohesive, and he should know that our nation has not bowed to force and will make aggressors regret it." @VahidOnLive

📡 @VahidOnline

🔰 Documenting the Lives of 500 Martyrs on Radio

🔸On the eve of commemorating Sacred Defense Week, a ceremony was held to unveil the 200-episode radio documentary series "Yaqut," produced by the Health Radio Network.

🔸According to a Kayhan reporter, Ahmad Pahlavanian, Deputy of Voice of the Islamic Republic of Iran, spoke at the ceremony, honoring the exalted status of the families of martyrs: "So far, the lives of more than 500 exalted martyrs have been documented and recorded on radio, and this path continues with strength."

🔸Paying tribute to the radio martyrs of the "Ramadan War" — martyrs Sadra Redaei and Farzad Mahdavi from Radio Namayesh — he emphasized: "Narrating the lives of martyrs in series such as 'Yaqut' is not merely a retelling of past memories, but an opportunity to come to know human beings who made great choices at critical moments. The national media has a duty to revisit these true role models for today's and future generations through accurate and artistic narration."

🔸Hojjat al-Islam Seyyed Ramazan Mousavimoghaddam, representative of the Supreme Leader in the Foundation of Martyrs and Veterans Affairs, also expressed appreciation for the national media's work in finding subjects and producing magnificent documentaries, saying: "Many untold dimensions of the martyrs' sacrifice remain that must be explained. The martyrs, by giving their lives, gifted health of spirit and body to society, and from this perspective, all martyrs are 'health martyrs.'" In continuation of this ceremony, Vahid Jalili, Cultural Deputy of the Head of the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting, stating that narrating the martyrs is in truth a manifestation of the remembrance of God, added: "Keeping alive the memory of the martyrs injects true vitality and hope into society, because the path of the martyrs is free of fear and discouragement."

🔸At the end of this ceremony, while honoring the Bahanar movement (child of the precious martyr Ayatollah Mohammad Javad Bahanar), the families of the exalted martyrs of radio and the production crew of the documentary, the collection of 200 radio documentaries "Yaqut" was unveiled.

entry.title: [VahidOnline] A senior official of the Islamic Republic has said Tehran has proposed that if…
entry.summary:

Source: @VahidOnline

A senior official of the Islamic Republic has said Tehran has proposed that if the United States reduces military pressure and takes initial steps to end the blockade of Iran's ports, it will reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and return to negotiations with Washington. The Kyodo news agency reported on Tuesday, 31 Shahrivar 1405, citing this official, whose name was not disclosed, that the proposal was conveyed to the U.S. government through intermediaries and is part of Tehran's new effort to revive negotiations with Washington. Under the proposal, the Islamic Republic is seeking to resume negotiations aimed at reaching an agreement for a "permanent end to hostilities" between Iran and the United States. The official said that in the first phase, Tehran expects Washington to show signs of readiness to return to negotiations and to begin taking measures to end the military blockade of Iran's ports and halt military operations related to the Strait of Hormuz. If these steps are taken, the Islamic Republic is prepared to open the shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and return to the negotiating table. The official stressed that America must demonstrate its "seriousness and commitment" for diplomacy to move forward. Kyodo reported that Tehran's new proposal has been approved by "Mojtaba Khamenei," the Leader of the Islamic Republic, and the Supreme National Security Council. The Iranian official did not specify whether the proposal means Tehran is backing away from part of the seven conditions previously put forward for negotiations and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. According to Kyodo's report, the Supreme National Security Council had decided on 25 Mordad that if America does not end the blockade of Iran's ports within 45 days, the Islamic Republic would reserve the option of attacking American forces again. That deadline is now approaching. At the same time, a senior Iranian official has told "Reuters" that the Islamic Republic's delegation at the United Nations General Assembly in New York has full authority to revive diplomatic talks with America, and the details of a possible agreement can be discussed through mediating countries in New York. The Iranian official ruled out the possibility of a meeting between "Masoud Pezeshkian" and "Donald Trump" on the sidelines of the General Assembly, but said that "the possibility of moving toward an agreement" still exists. @VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline

🔸 The twenty-first of September each year, which in the Solar Hijri calendar usually falls on the 30th of Shahrivar, has been designated the International Day of Peace.
🔸 By proclaiming this day, the United Nations calls on nations and governments to observe a full day of ceasefire and to promote a culture of peace. Yet on the very same days when these slogans are repeated, Western fighter jets soar over various parts of the world, and weapons shipments pour from the ports of countries that claim to champion peace into conflict zones. The contradiction between rhetoric and action lays bare, more than anything else, the dual nature of the Western order.
🔸 Ultimately, the impact of this double standard on future generations in war-torn regions is a subject rarely touched upon in the official ceremonies of the Day of Peace. Yashar and Farnaz, in pursuit of scapegoating Iran
🔹In the middle of his exposé clip about the trusts, Yashar Soltani — without mentioning America's prior violations — names the Stability political faction as the cause of the understanding's collapse.
🔹This is the same narrative previously put forward in Farnaz Fassihi's report in the New York Times; a narrative claiming that the action of a rogue group in Iran destroyed the diplomatic opportunity that existed in the understanding between Iran and America.
But what is the hidden reality?
🔹The most important clause of the understanding was the acceptance of Iranian arrangements in the administration of the strait. That is, in exchange for accepting certain obligations, Iran had secured its right to manage and maintain its own particular arrangements in the world's most important oil passage.
🔹From day one, America was determined to violate this clause and, as with the violation of other clauses, to normalize it. The failure to release the assets and the failure to establish a ceasefire on other fronts are clear examples of these violations.
🔹Logically, Iran, in defense of its gains under the understanding, should have shown itself to be serious and, during the transitional period, should have stood firm on its rights so that it could secure its right in the final agreement.
🔹The opening of the southern corridor in the strait was a fundamental violation of the understanding by America — an action that, if left unanswered, would have practically rendered the main clause of the understanding ineffective.
🔹After several days of warnings, the timely action of striking the vessels and not remaining indifferent to the violation of Iran's rights under the understanding was defensible on the part of the country's decision-makers.
🔹The inverted narrative of the story that portrays Iran as responsible for disrupting the understanding is fabricated by Israeli and monarchist accounts and American media.
Why is this narrative important?
🔸If this reading is correct, what happened in the Strait of Hormuz was a reaction to America's clear violation of the understanding.
🔸In this framework, the one who first broke the understanding was Washington, not Iran. But the rival narrative, by swapping the roles of victim and culprit, wants to shift the political cost of this decision onto an internal faction.
🔸The narrative that "the rogues broke the understanding" is on the surface simple and attractive, but when placed alongside America's chain of violations, it collapses.
🖼The important question, however, is why should one expect Iran to remain a spectator in the face of the violation of the main clause of the understanding? And why now, instead of condemning the primary violator, is the finger of accusation pointed inward?

📢 The inevitable shift in Iranian tastes; red meat consumption drops to one-third

◀️ The Donya-e-Eqtesad newspaper has reported a significant change in the meat consumption patterns of Iranian households. According to the report, per capita red meat consumption has fallen from about 14 kilograms in the mid-1380s to roughly 5 kilograms in recent years.

◀️ At the same time, households have increasingly turned to chicken to make up for reduced access to red meat, with chicken's share of total meat consumption rising from about 30 percent in the 1360s to around 60 percent. That figure is said to be less than 30 percent globally.

◀️ Total per capita meat consumption has also dropped from about 35 kilograms in 1383 to 25 kilograms in 1403 — a decline of roughly 30 percent.

◀️ Donya-e-Eqtesad stressed that this trend cannot be attributed solely to a "change in taste"; the decline in households' real income and the surge in food prices have also played a major role. According to the report, meat prices rose about 5.8 times between 1400 and 1404.

🔸The military news agency 19forty five wrote in its latest piece:

The White House has informed Congress that it intends to sell 30 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia in a $24 billion contract. The timing of this decision is no accident; after the drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and the Yemeni forces' capture of Al-Mokha, Riyadh's ability to export oil via the Red Sea has been jeopardized. Mohammed bin Salman is in one of the toughest crises of his time.

🔸Congress has serious concerns. The F-35 sale may violate Washington's commitment to maintaining the Zionist regime's qualitative military edge. For half a century, America has guaranteed that Israel maintains its technological superiority over its Arab neighbors. But Saudi Arabia's closeness to China and Turkey and its membership in BRICS have raised serious questions about trust in Riyadh. If Turkey was expelled from the F-35 program over its purchase of the S-400 system, why should Saudi Arabia get a free pass? These factors do not necessarily make Riyadh an enemy of America, but bin Salman's double-dealing is not something the US government can trust.

🔸The F-35 will not solve the Saudis' problem against the Houthis. Over the past 12 years, Saudi Arabia has been unable to contain the Yemeni forces through air power. The attack on Al-Mokha airport after the Yemeni forces' takeover was merely a military propaganda stunt. By selling these advanced American fighter jets, Trump and bin Salman can convince their publics that they have taken effective measures — while the delivery and training of the F-35 takes years, or even a decade.

🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram

🔸 The recent remarks by the spokesman of the Parliament's National Security Commission pulled back the curtain on a massive miscalculation — where "naivety" had taken the place of rationality. Hassan Qashqavi announced that before the start of the 12-day war and during three rounds of Geneva negotiations, Iran "offered an economic cooperation proposal worth approximately $500 billion to American companies." He emphasized that "this proposal was drawn up in various sectors including oil and gas, mining, environment, and transportation, and economic officials and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs were present at the negotiations to present these capacities." Referring to this delusional proposal, Qashqavi stated that "the goal was to pave the way for cooperation between American companies and Iran by showcasing economic opportunities and profitability." But the bitter truth was that Washington had long since sharpened its teeth to dismember and devour Iran. According to the spokesman of the National Security Commission, "this proposal was based on the assumption that Trump's business approach could change upon seeing economic interests; but in the end, even offering a $500 billion cooperation proposal did not prevent the outbreak of tension and war."

🔸 This failed pipe dream was the product of the delusions of an incompetent faction that has been running the country with wrong directions for years. Along the same lines, Hossein Marashi, Secretary-General of Kargozaran Sazandegi, had also made a bizarre claim: "Iran has a total investment capacity of about $2,500 billion; a capacity that, if activated, could set the engine of Iran's economy and even the region's economy in motion." 🔰An explosion in the oil market with a single matchstick/Why is now the best time for an oil price surge?🔸According to an International Energy Agency report, at the start of the Ramadan war, the world's oil reserves—both offshore and onshore—exceeded 8.2 billion barrels.🔸Given the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, JPMorgan presented its forecast for the decline in global oil reserves as follows: in June, reserve levels reach 7.68 billion barrels, which is the "operational stress" level.🔸Then in September, global oil reserves reach 6.8 billion barrels—the "operational floor"—which would completely disrupt refinery operations.🔸Unfortunately, JPMorgan's forecast for the timing of these two events did not materialize; the drawdown of oil reserves proceeded more slowly and now stands at about 7.7 billion barrels.🔸Of course, had 250 million barrels of non-Iranian oil not passed through the Strait of Hormuz under the Islamabad understanding, and had the Iranian side not then turned a blind eye—hoping for the agreement's revival—to more than 350 million barrels of oil passing through the Omani route, JPMorgan's forecast would have come true.🔸But in any case, reserve levels have now reached about 7.7 billion barrels, close to the "operational stress" level. As a result, the conditions for Iran to drive an oil price surge have actually become more favorable now.🔸That is, by injecting even the smallest tension or risk into the oil market, the price can suddenly be sent soaring. The least Iran can do is shut down the 5-million-barrel leak of oil passing through the Strait of Hormuz.🔸Iran has less than two months until the U.S. midterm elections to send oil prices surging—this opportunity must not be squandered on the fantasy of a paper agreement.🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online

📍America's inflation expectations have become tied to the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab

🔖In a tweet, Ghalibaf preemptively dismissed today's much-hyped decision by the US central bank on interest rates as inconsequential regardless of its outcome, writing:

📌Let's see whether the Federal Reserve can open the Strait of Hormuz or produce even one more barrel of oil by raising interest rates?!

📌You can't manage (anchor) inflation expectations in America by raising and lowering interest rates, because those expectations are driven by the supply-side shock caused by the blockage of energy chokepoints — namely the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab — and have nothing to do with interest rates. It is the "Strait of Hormuz risk" that determines the rate, and control over that risk now lies with Iran.

📌Ghalibaf's emphasis in this post is on the idea that the era of managing inflation and inflation expectations using demand-side tools alone (interest rates) is over, and that it is geopolitics that now holds the upper hand in shaping economic indicators such as inflation.

📌Under normal conditions, a central bank traditionally seeks to anchor inflation expectations to its inflation target or to a credible long-term inflation rate in order to contain inflation, and it achieves this anchoring by adjusting interest rates in line with the inflation target and the economy's distance from full capacity.

📌But in this post, the Parliament Speaker, by upending the classic formula for setting interest rates in America, warns market participants that tinkering with interest rates will not achieve the goal of containing inflation in America, and that they must factor new variables into their calculations — such as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab — and accept that circumstances have changed: unless Iran wills it, inflation expectations in America will not be anchorable, and inflation will keep climbing.
